properties.title: PA Permit Violation Issued to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming County
properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/06/2024 to EQT ARO LLC in Plunketts Creek Township, Lycoming county. CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: EQT ARO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 6/06/2024
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 8190155
Permit API: 081-21946
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Plunketts Creek Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/06/2024
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator of the discovery of a release of an estimated 20 gallons of a mixture of produced fluid and fresh water. According to the notification, fluid with electrical conductivity (EC) of 10-13 mS/cm was discovered on the pad surface in an area southeast of the well heads when secondary containment was removed from the pad surface. The notification also stated that a shallow trench has been dug along the southeast edge of the secondary containment to collect any additional fluid with elevated EC that may leach out from beneath the containment. The area impacted by the release was estimated to be 30 ft by 50 ft. I met with company man Steven Spitler upon arriving on location. It rained heavily during this inspection. The EC of the fluid present in the trench along the southeast edge of the well head secondary containment was between 4.03 mS/cm and 5.06 mS/cm. The 30 ft by 50 ft area of the pad surface reported to have been impacted by the release southeast of the well heads had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 2.48 mS/cm and 4.00 mS/cm. A vaccum truck was sucking up fluid from the impacted area of the pad surface during this inspection. Other areas of the pad surface had puddles of fluid with EC readings between 856 uS/cm to 1990 uS/cm. According to the company man, excavation of this area was going to be completed by Tobias Machining, present on site during this inspection, and characterization of the site would be conducted by Penn E and R who was en-route to the site during this inspection. The Department requests a justification for the estimated release volume. The Department recommends continuing to vacuum up fluid with elevated EC from the pad surface. Violations noted against permit 081-21945 for the 6/6/24 reported release. Violations remain outstanding against permit 081-21946 for the 5/8/24 release discovered by the Department. These violations will be closed upon attainment of Act 2 remediation standards.

OGA3216(C) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PITS, DRILLING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT - Failure to fill all pits used to contain produced fluids or industrial wastes and remove unnecessary drilling supplies/equipment not needed for production within 9 months from completion of drilling of well.
properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: OGA3216(C) - WELL SITE RESTORATIONS - PITS, DRILLING SUPPLIES AND EQUIPMENT - Failure to fill all pits used to contain produced fluids or industrial wastes and remove unnecessary drilling supplies/equipment not needed for production within 9 months from completion of drilling of well.
Violation ID: 8154325
Permit API: 121-45433
Unconventional: No
County: Venango
Municipality: Sugarcreek Borough
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 8/03/2023
Comments: Onsite to investigate Complaint # 373782 dated 7/20/2023 and a follow-up inspection to Inspection Report # 3589928 dated 7/21/2023. Onsite with DEP staff Alicia Furey and Lucas Eichner to collect a water sample from the earthen dike. The earthen dike is retaining fluid inside the bottom of the entire dike. There is approximately 4-5" of oily water pooled inside the dike. The dike drain remains closed and plugged. Water flowing into a separator barrel on top of a steel oil tank could be heard from the ground.Prior to the site visit water samples of the Bellows Spring was collected for analysis. There are 4 separate pipes flowing water into the cistern for the spring. Each pipe was identified, labeled, and sampled separately.After collecting samples from the earthen dike, DEP staff walked the hillside between the tank battery and Bellows Spring. The goal was to investigate any other oil and gas activity that may be located above the spring and that would be a potential contributor to the impact of the Bellows Spring. There was nothing observed between the tank battery and the Bellows Spring relating to oil and gas activity.At 2:05pm Mr. Rhoades was called via phone by the Department. The current condition of the tank battery was discussed with Mr. Rhoades and he indicated that a water truck is scheduled for next week to empty the dike and the brine tanks. Mr. Rhoades also stated that he has hired Moody and Associates as a consultant and that a check was in the mail to obtain their services. The Department clearly communicated the importance and urgency of starting the cleanup process at the site including the earthen dike area. Mr. Rhoades seemed to understand and asked if the water was good to drink yet in Reno and if individual households are being tested. I explained to Mr. Rhoades that samples have been taken from the spring by Oil and Gas Operations and that I was unaware of any other sampling/testing. It was also stated that the "Do not Consume" advisory has not yet been lifted from my knowledge at the time. The phone call was concluded with Mr. Rhoades indicating that he is starting the process to clean things up.

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 2/10/2026
Comments: On 02/10/2026, an incident inspection was conducted following notification of a spill that occurred on 2/09/2026 from Greylock (CTS #395045). I was accompanied by Madison Raviart (PA DEP Water Quality Specialist) and Greylock representative Trevor Wood. Per Greylock, the spill was reported to the Department's emergency hotline on 02/09/2026. It was reported that 1-3 bbls of brine water released onto the pad on 02/09/2026. The spill was identified at 4:00 PM and reported to the hotline at approximately 7:13 PM. Gravel and snow was impacted on the pad and the spill was contained to the pad and snow was hand shoveled into tanks containment. No waters of the Commonwealth were impacted. The following was observed during the inspection:The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance. There was no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite at the site entrance (Photo 1). I recommend these be added to site near the site entrance. The access road appeared to be in generally good condition and maintained (Photo 2).Cinders were placed on road coming up to the pad on 02/10/2026 (Photos 3-5). Snow around the containment for the tanks was hand shoveled and put into the containment (Photo 6). The spill originated from a separator on the pad. High pressure caused brine water to come out of the separator and spray onto the pad and tank. 1-3 barrels (bbls) were released (Photos 7-10). Conductivity readings taken in the middle of the impacted area ranged from 2.09 mS/cm-4.55mS/cm (Photos 11,12). Conductivity reading taken in gravel on the opposite side of the entrance in front of separators was 252 S/cm (Photo 13). Conductivity readings taken along tank containment ranged from 709 S/cm-8.61 mS/cm (Photos 14-18).The area was still in the process of remediation and Greylock was waiting on additional equipment to begin remediation. The spill appeared to be greater than 42 gallons. I recommend following Act 2 guidelines.Due to the release of brine water and no Emergency Response Plan or The Preparedness, Prevention, and Contingency plan onsite, violations of 78a.54, 78a57(a), SWMA 301, 91.34(a), 78A55(I)5I, and 78a66(b)2.

Comments: Incident inspection of Chesapeake's "Rocks" Marcellus shale well site. The ESCGP covers 3 separate Marcellus sites. This inspection only covers "Rocks" (not Dryscoll or Oil Can).Danielle Schaad called the DEP on Monday January 27, 2025 to report an estimated 5 gallon release of produced liquid from a hammer union to the pad surface. The release occurred during flowback operations that day. Some of the liquid flowed under liner containment for GasBuster tanks, so they removed 2 of the Gasbusters and part of the liner on January 28 to be able to excavate impacted material. I spoke with Andy Steffe and Tiffany Smith (both Creston Environmental) on site. During this inspection they collected field screening soil samples from the edges of the excavated area in glass jars and mixed in distilled water to make a slurry. The 16 samples returned electrical conductivity (EC) readings of 0.02-1.65 mS/cm with a YSI meter. Only 1 of the jars returned EC >1.0 mS/cm. A track hoe removed pad material from the spot that was 1.65 mS/cm during this inspection. The removed pad material is placed on liner containment on the SW corner of the pad. Creston will also send soil samples to a lab today to comply with Act 2 Cleanups, since the volume of the release is unknown. They plan on backfilling the excavated area today after sampling.Danielle Schaad messaged that they covered the waste pile with plastic. The excavated area was approximately 43'x32'x2' deep which equals 125 cubic yards; they backfilled it today after my inspection.Violations are cited to the 015-23897 permit.Precision Drilling 573 drilled the 3 new Marcellus wells here on February-March, 2024. Universal hydraulically fractured the 3 new Marcellus wells here in July 2024.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site, but cannot fully assess stabilization because of partial snow cover. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls are in place and appear to be functioning as designed.I did not see any pooled water on the pad surface, just snow. Moist soil on the pad has electrical conductivity of 0.72 mS/cm with a Hanna Soil Test.Air temp 27FJLP

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 2020-05-22 to Dorso Lp in New Stanton Boro, Westmoreland county. 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
properties.content:
Report Details
Operator: Dorso Lp
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 2020-05-22
Violation Code: 102.4(b)1 - EROSION AND SEDIMENT CONTROL REQUIREMENTS - Person conducting earth disturbance activity failed to implement and maintain E & S BMPs to minimize the potential for accelerated erosion and sedimentation.
Violation ID: 885702
Permit API: 129-26159
Unconventional: No
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: New Stanton Boro
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 2020-05-22
Comments: This inspection is being conducted as a follow up to IR 2997935 conducted on 2/14/2020 in which violations were issued. The entirety of the site was walked due to a pad lock on the gate (Photo 2). The access road still appears to be rutted which in several locations has allowed for the creation of accelerated erosion channels (Photo 1, 6, 11, 12, 13, 16, 17, & 27). Straw bale barriers still appear to be installed incorrectly and not properly maintained (Photo 4, 5, 9, 10, 14, 15, 18, & 19). The access road is still pooling water at low spots, this has created the potential for sediment discharges leaving the site (Photo 3, 8, 14, 18). In several locations the water has been standing long enough for tad poles to occupy them (Photo 20). No E&S Plan was found on site. Per the E&S Plan received in the operator's response dated 2/24/2020 and created in 2006, it appears that at least one culvert that was installed is not depicted on their plan, nor is it installed to the details set forth in that E&S Plan (Photo 7). Per 102.4(b)8 the E&S Plan must be available for review at the project site during all stages of earth disturbance activity. The access road and well pad do not have adequate temporary stabilization, nor have they achieved a minimum uniform 70% vegetative cover (Photo 1, 8, 11, 12, 13, 16, 22, 24, & 25). Down slope controls at the well site, do not appear to have been installed (Photo 23). Based on this inspection, violations will be issued as reoccurring for potential for discharge, and failure to have the site temporary stabilized, additional violations will remain outstanding.

According to the COA, Diversified is to restore the Well Site in accordance with Section 3216 of the 2012 Oil and Gas Act 58 Pa. C.S.A. 3216.According to Department records, this well was plugged on 3/20/2025, therefore the well site should be fully restored by 12/20/2025 and a well site restoration report be submitted to the Department by 2/18/2026 or a well site restoration extension request should be submitted by 9/20/2025 (6 months after the plugging of the well). IR 4115541 documents the return of a 12/19/2025 submitted well site restoration extension request and IR 4156187 documents the return of a 2/25/2026 submitted well site restoration report which did not include a Post-Plugging Landowner Waiver of Site Restoration requesting the access road remain.At the time of this inspection, the Department observed an unrestored dirt/gravel access road leading to the Dinunno 1 plugged well site. No site restoration plan for plugging was observed to be available on site. The Department recommends the site restoration plan be available on site during all stages of earth disturbance activity in accordance with 102.4b8. Violations were issued during IR 4156187 for failure to have a post-plugging site restoration plan on site.At the time of this inspection, the Department traveled to the plugged well's coordinate GPS location and did not observe any fluid leaks or fluid dischages at the surface of the plugged well's approximate location. At the time of this inspection, the well site appeared to be exhibiting 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth with no erosion and sedimentation issues observed. The CFS (Compost Filter Sock) that was previously observed to be installed on site appeared to be spread along the perimeters of the plugged well site. At the time of this inspection, the Department still observed what appears to be a graveled channel along the edge of the well site. The Department was unable to determine if this channel is associated with the plugged well site or not due to the Site Restoration Plan not being on site. No production equipment appeared to be on site at the time of this inspection.Based on today's inspection, it appears that the access road is not restored as it remains. Restoration of the well site cannot be confirmed due to the post-plugging restoration plan not being on-site. Violations are being continued for failure to comply with an COA of the Department for failure to restore by 12/20/2025 - 9 months from plugging.

Comments: On April 25, 2025, an inspection was conducted at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. The purpose of this inspection was to follow up to IR 3965337, where violations were issued in response to an estimated 50 barrel release of a brine/crude oil mixture. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth were observed during the time of IR 3965337.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who stated that forecasted storms have delayed start of remediation to Monday, 4/28/2025. In response, the impacted area was covered, and oil absorbent booms and E and S controls were installed downslope.The following was observed:The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photos 5 and 6). The path of brown staining that was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank has been covered with plastic sheeting in preparation for the forecasted rains. Additional oil absorbent booms have also been placed down slope of the covered impacted area (see photos 8-15). No evidence of visual impacts and/or elevated conductivity were detected down slope of impacted area (see photos 16 and 17).Based on observations from this inspection, it appears that the impacted area has been adequately,protected to mitigate risk of the impact being spread by stormwater.Violations issued from IR 3965337 shall remain outstanding.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/25/2026 to REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC in Pike Township, Bradford county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: REPSOL OIL & GAS USA LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/25/2026
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8268727
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 3/25/2026
Comments: On 03/24/2026 at 1132 hours Repsol reported (CTS#396090) that at 0600 hours they noticed fluid in the southside ditch of the Ugliuzza well pad that was going towards the catch basin. There was a hose that did not have a cap on it and the fluid was coming from the hose. They are estimating ~630 gallons (1 barrel=42 gallons) of produced water was released off containment. Resource Management was contracted to conduct remediation. At ~1525 hours Repsol contacted the DEP to update the amount release to be ~18,900 gallons. Four water trucks off-loading onsite each contained 4,620 gallons of produced fluid. It is estimated that the release traveled 1,143 feet downhill to the stream. A remediation plan is in place, and they are implementing it as we spoke. On 03/23/2026 at 2218 hours the first of five water trucks arrived onsite to off-load fluid for upcoming completion activities. From 2218-0319 hours 4 water trucks off-loaded onsite. At 0615 hours on 03/24/2026 a 5th water truck started offloading and immediately noticed the leak and stopped off-loading. On 03/25/2026 Repsol reported that as of 0700 hours ~10,500 gallons of fluid had been recovered from the stormwater channel and basin. On 03/25/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection report of Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad. Water Quality Specialists Korey Starkey, Jonathan Pennings and I arrived at ~ 0930 hours. Licensed Professional Geologist Samuel Louderback arrived at approximately 1100 hours. The DEP met with Repsol representative Meagan DePue and Resource Management. Fenton Excavation was onsite excavating within the LOD to capture fluids during the inspection. Meagan stated that she contacted the PFBC and left a message. She informed us that a hose connected to the manifold was not connected to the produced fluid tanks and that it was hanging over the side of the secondary containment into the stormwater ditch while the first four trucks off-loaded (photo #2-6). The produced fluid then flowed to the stormwater basin (photo #7) and through the drainage pipe of the stormwater basin (photo #9) into a natural conveyance channel which reached a UNT to Rockwell Creek. The DEP, Repsol and Resource Management walked the impacted area together. Resource Management set up monitoring points and split sampled during that time. The fluids in the stormwater ditch were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) at ~7.85 mS/cm. There was a sump pump in the stormwater ditch (photo #5). A sample was collected from the stormwater basin at 1204 hours (photo #8). The EC of the sampled fluids were >19.99 mS/cm. Fluids were able to escape the basin through an outflow pipe. Two sumps were constructed inside and outside of the basin (photo #7 and 10). Fluids collected in the sumps were being actively recovered.The EC of the drainage area beyond the stormwater basin was ~1.8 mS/cm and the soil EC was ~4.8 mS/cm (photo #11). The drainage area forms a conveyance channel ~500ft down from the release location. The EC of the conveyance channel was ~5.4 mS/cm (photo #12). There was a spring adding water to the channel ~900ft downstream from the release location. It was located above grade (photo #13). The EC of the spring was ~100 us/cm. We traveled ~500ft downstream the conveyance channel and obtained EC readings between 2.6-2.7 mS/cm (photo #14 and 15).We traveled downstream ~435ft. The conveyance channel EC was between 5.8-8.0 mS/cm (photo #16 and 17). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1053 hours from the UNT upstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #18). The DEP and Resource Management each collected a sample at 1118 hours from the UNT downstream of where the released fluids discharged into the stream (photo #22).The EC of Rockwell Creek ~1.4 miles away was ~0.15 mS/cm.

Comments: On 02/14/2020 WQS Kristof Eichenlaub conducted incident response inspection # 2999089 On 02/18/2020 at approximately 1350 I conducted a follow up inspection at the site. Foamer product and sediment laden water were discharging from the sediment basin outlet, overwhelming two silt socks, and discharging outside the LOD into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. The discharge caused accelerated erosion below the silt socks and extending into UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A contractor for Greylock was utilizing a bucket and a pressurized sprayer bottle in an attempt to remove foamer product from the sediment basin rip rap outlet. I contacted Greylock Regulatory Compliance Coordinator Keith Eighmey via phone, who indicated he was unaware of the contractor's activities. The Department requests Greylock provide the SDS for the defoaming agent. The spill had not been remediated and was continuing to discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run. A sediment laden water discharge to UNT 8 to Frosty Run was also continuing. Greylock discharged an additional substance to Waters of the Commonwealth during their attempt to remove the foamer. Some violations are ongoing as a result of a spill that was documented on 02/14/2020 (inspection # 2999089). Additional violations of CSL 301 and 307 have occurred due to Greylock discharging a chemical to UNT 8 to reduce the surfactant foam. A violation of OGA3259(2I) has occurred for failure to comply with DEP cleanup order issued on 02/14/2020.

An Act 9 sign remains at the entrance to the well site.I met with the Repsol representative who reported to the DEP that on Friday, 4/21/2023, an unknown quantity of rainwater released off the edge of the pad surface from a tear in a secondary containment structure. One additional preexisting well remains capable of production. Numerous temporary storage containers are held within secondary containment onsite. Pooled water on the pad surface that was field measured for electrical conductivity ranged from 220 to 750us/cm today. There was no evidence of spills/releases observed. Violations cited against API #015-23745 on 12/20/2022 and 12/28/2022 remain outstanding at this time. No additional violations are cited at this time. The DEP requests the analytical sample results from the samples collected related to the stormwater release. I departed the site at 1140 hours.

Comments: On January 10, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at STL Resources Sturgis South Pad in response to a spill notification received on January 10, 2022. DEP spoke with Seth Rodriguez with STL Resources. Mr. Rodriguez said that a hose that manifolded multiple frac tanks onsite broke and released approximately 1,600 barrels of production fluid water from frac tanks. There were 17 frac tanks onsite in secondary containment for flow back storage from recent stimulation of the wells on the pad. The secondary containment of the frac tanks was overwhelmed and some of the production fluid water spilled to the pad surface. The amount of production fluid that was spilled to the pad surface is still being calculated. The spill was first noticed on January 8, 2022 but STL Resources failed to notify the DEP emergency spill line. The production fluid ran into a drain on the southwest corner of the well pad which outlets off the pad into a infiltration berm. An area 60 yds. x 40 yds. of the pad surface was impacted by production fluid. Off the pad area of impact was about 20 ft. wide by 120 ft. long. At the time of inspection, STL Resources contractors were vacuuming up the free standing production fluid out of the drainage outlet and the fluid pooled up in front of the infiltration berm. The DEP measured soil conductivity around the area of impact on the well pad and multiple measurements resulted in over range readings of the soil conductivity meter. Soil conductivity off the pad surface where the production fluid water flowed into the infiltration berm also resulted in an over range readings. Comments: This inspection is in response to a complaint of a spill on 03/07/2022 located at the Armac lease on Bauer Hill road. The complainant reported a strong smell and saw diapers and oil booms in the Bauer Hill road ditch as well as inside the containment diking. Upon responding to the complaint, and speaking with Vince Bailey the pumper for the lease he reported that the storage tank had over flowed on Saturday March 5th, he cleaned up the oil inside containment he estimated the spill at 2.5 barrels. Monday crude oil had breached the diking by migrating through the pervious material used in the construction of the containment. The crude oil flowed down slope approx 250 feet into a road side ditch on Bauer Hill road, it continued another 275 feet into an unnamed tributary (UNT) of Glade Run. Violation ID: 965910
Permit API: 015-23728
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Monroe Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 8/23/2022
Comments: Inspection of Chesapeake's "Jads" Marcellus well site.Aaron Stredny (Chesapeake) called the DEP on Friday August 19, 2022 to report an estimated 50 gallon spill of diesel fuel. The spill happened when a fuel tank fell off a forklift. A vac truck already on site removed the standing liquid fuel, they also used absorbent pads on the fuel.I spoke with Danny Lambert (Company Man) on site. He showed me where the fuel spill occurred, which is now a water puddle. I did not see any sheen or evidence of residual fuel on the pad. A MiniRae 3000 photoionization detector with a 10.6 eV bulb returned 0.0 ppm readings from the spill area, indicating absence of volatiles emitting from that area. Creston Environmental is arriving tomorrow to delineate the impacted pad area for excavation and sampling. Nabors' X25 rig is installing production casing in the the 3rd of 6 Marcellus wells here today. Tomorrow they start drilling the 4th well. They drill on water/bentonite until ~7,000' depth, then switch to diesel based mud for "kickoff" into the horizontal section. Lambert expects to finish drilling here in October 2022.Vegetation and rock stabilize soil of the site. I did not see accelerated erosion or sedimentation.Containment structures are intact. I did not observe any leaks or other deficiencies.I did not see any Post Construction Stormwater Management (PCSM) controls in place.Pooled on the pad surface in 5 separate areas has electrical conductivity of 0.46-0.67 mS/cm with an Oakton PCSTestr 35. Air temp 79FJLP
